method: Landed cost per watt of a TOPCon module at a US port = FOB price + ocean freight + duties on the customs (FOB) value. Duties stack: AD and CVD cash deposit rates (all-others or country-wide, latest stage on file in data/tracker.json), Section 301 on China (50%), the forced-labour Section 301 flat rate (10% or 12.5% by country, from 24 Jul 2026), and from 4 Dec 2026 the Section 232 action on polysilicon derivatives (15% plus a minimum import price of $0.38/W for modules; the shortfall below the MIP is collected as a specific duty). Prices are public spot assessments, not quotes, and Southeast Asian origins share one published bucket. Every input below carries its source and date; change the inputs on the page to test your own numbers.
notes: InfoLink and OPIS publish one 'Southeast Asia made' module price, not a price per country; Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia and Laos therefore start from the same FOB figure here, and Laos is flagged because no Laos-specific assessment exists.
Public cell prices by origin are not published outside China (InfoLink's SEA, India and US cell rows are paywalled), so this page prices modules only.

Whether the forced-labour Section 301 rate keeps applying to cells and modules once they become Section 232 articles on 4 Dec 2026 is not settled in public guidance (the 301 notice exempts Section 232 articles in general; law-firm summaries read the two as additive). The page lets you switch it off.

IEEPA tariffs were struck down by the Supreme Court on 20 Feb 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on 24 Jul 2026; neither is in the stack. The Section 201 safeguard expired on 6 Feb 2026.
Freight is derived: the Drewry Shanghai to Los Angeles 40 ft rate divided by the watts in a 40 ft HQ container of 580 W modules (620 modules). Other lanes are not published on Drewry's public page.
